audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer tracks 'Twofold Hunt' — Aurora's Q is Twofold Hex. It also calls the tracked ability 'her escape' and 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)', conflating her poke with her escape. Separately, the content layer calls Across the Veil 'untargetable' and gives Twofold Hex a 'double-hit immobilize'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Twofold Hex (Q, 900 range, 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s) is a curse missile with a recast that drags curses back — no CC in the description and no slow/hardCC flag. Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18s) is a leap that makes her invisible, which is not the same as untargetable. The Weirding (E, 15/14/13/12/11s) is the blast that hops her backward. Her escape is W; her poke is Q.
audit.corrected: Tracked ability is Across the Veil (22s) where the text means her escape and Twofold Hex where it means her poke; 'untargetable' corrected to invisible; the unsupported immobilize replaced with the real recast-drag.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] said Twofold Hex out-ranges Gnar's Mini kite. It does not. whys[5] and whys[6] also contradicted their own chart entries (her AP item spike scored as Gnar; 'it levels out' scored as Gnar).
audit.why: Boomerang Throw is 1100 range against Twofold Hex's 900 — Gnar wins the pure spacing war in Mini form, which is exactly what the Aurora-side mirror recorded when it kept levels 2-3 Gnar-sided. Her first AP item is a genuine Aurora stage, and two items is the stage the prose itself calls even.
audit.corrected: Level 3 stays Gnar (mirror-consistent) with the range numbers stated; first item -> Aurora; 2+ items -> Skill.

audit.why: Aurora's spikes are level 6 (Between Worlds, 140/120/100s) and her first AP item; Gnar's is 'Mega up', which spikes[3].when already labels correctly rather than pinning it to level 6. Between Worlds is a 140s zone at rank 1 and GNAR! is 90s falling to 30s, matching the mirror's finding.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions Grievous Wounds despite Spirit Abjuration healing her off every spell and attack that damages you.
audit.why: Her passive heals from spirits exorcised by damage she deals, so a long poke war refills her; Executioner's Calling / Oblivion Orb is what makes chip damage stick.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal added to the itemization line.

notes: 'Twofold Hunt' is fabricated (real: Twofold Hex) and was the tracked ability across the full layer; where the text meant her escape I retargeted it to Across the Veil, which is what a Gnar actually has to bait. Two claims in the content layer were unsupported and are corrected rather than repeated: Across the Veil makes her invisible, not untargetable, and Riot's Twofold Hex text describes no immobilize (no slow or hardCC flag either) — the recast drags the curse back for damage. I kept level 3 Gnar-sided to stay consistent with the Aurora-side mirror and rewrote its why with the 1100-vs-900 range fact the mirror established. QUESTION-FREE: nothing skipped.
